title: Sell Mineral Rights in Weld County, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Weld County, CO | DJ Basin Core
metaDescription: Weld County is Colorado's top oil-producing county and the heart of the Wattenberg Field. Get a comp-based cash offer on your Niobrara or Codell interest.
heroLead: Weld County produces more oil than any other county in Colorado, and it's the single most consistent market we work in for Niobrara and Codell mineral interests.
intro: Weld County is the core of the Wattenberg Field and, by a wide margin, the largest oil-producing county in Colorado. Horizontal drilling into the Niobrara and Codell formations has run here continuously for more than a decade, laterals have stretched from one mile to two, three, and now sometimes four miles as operators consolidate acreage into fewer, larger pads. If you own minerals anywhere in Weld County, you're sitting in the state's most active and most closely watched oil and gas market, which is both an advantage and a reason to be precise about valuation.

That said, Weld County is a big place, and the difference between a tract in the deep Wattenberg core and one on the county's outer edge can be significant. Before we quote a number, we look at exactly where your section sits, what's currently producing around it, and what your division order actually shows.

sections.heading: A county that stayed open after SB 19-181
paragraphs: When Colorado passed SB 19-181 in 2019, giving local governments direct authority over oil and gas siting and shifting the state's regulatory mission toward public health and environmental protection, many Front Range municipalities responded by tightening local setbacks and permitting review. Weld County took a different path, working to become one of the state's designated Local Government Designees, which lets the county run its own expedited local review for oil and gas permits under COGCC's statewide framework rather than defaulting to slower state-level review.

The practical effect is that Weld County has stayed one of the more predictable places in Colorado to permit a new well, even as some of its own edge communities, and plenty of neighboring Adams and Broomfield-area suburbs, have adopted more cautious postures. That relative predictability is part of why operators like Civitas Resources and Oxy have continued to concentrate their Colorado drilling budgets here rather than spreading them thinner across the Front Range.

sections.heading: Who's operating in Weld County today
paragraphs: Civitas Resources, formed through the 2021 merger of Bonanza Creek, Extraction Oil & Gas, and Crestone Peak Resources and expanded further by its 2023 acquisition of PDC Energy, holds one of the largest positions in the Wattenberg Field. Occidental Petroleum, which inherited a major DJ Basin position through its 2019 acquisition of Anadarko, and Anadarko itself before that through Kerr-McGee's legacy Wattenberg holdings, is the other dominant operator across much of the county. Chevron also holds meaningful acreage.

Multi-well pad development is standard practice now, with operators drilling four, eight, sometimes more than a dozen wells from a single surface location to minimize surface disturbance and reach as many spacing units as possible from one pad. For a mineral owner, that means your specific tract's value increasingly depends on whether it falls inside a currently planned multi-well unit, not only whether oil and gas exists underneath it.

sections.heading: Split estate and the county's agricultural roots
paragraphs: Weld County was homesteaded and farmed for irrigated corn, sugar beets, and wheat long before the Niobrara became a household name in oil and gas circles. Many mineral owners today hold interests that trace back to those original farm families, sometimes retained when the surface sold, sometimes passed down through several generations of heirs with no direct connection to the land itself anymore.
That history means title work is rarely simple. We routinely find Weld County interests with a dozen or more heirs on record, and no two chains of title look exactly alike.

sections.heading: Forced pooling and small fractional owners
paragraphs: Because so much Weld County mineral ownership is fractionalized across heirs, forced pooling orders from the COGCC are a routine part of how operators assemble a horizontal spacing unit. If your interest was pooled, your division order should list a specific decimal share tied to a defined unit, and we verify that share against the underlying pooling order and current production data before making an offer.

sections.heading: What the Weld County Clerk and Recorder confirms
paragraphs: Every offer starts with the record. We pull your chain of title directly from the Weld County Clerk and Recorder in Greeley, confirm the mineral reservation survived every subsequent transfer, cross-reference your division order and any active lease, and only then price your interest against recent, comparable Wattenberg transactions rather than a flat countywide number.

faqs.question: Why is Weld County treated as the benchmark for DJ Basin pricing?
faqs.answer: It's the largest oil-producing county in the state and the deepest, most consistently developed part of the Wattenberg Field, so recent Weld County transactions are the most reliable comps we have for the broader DJ Basin.

faqs.question: Does it matter where in Weld County my tract sits?
faqs.answer: Yes, significantly. Deep-core Wattenberg acreage prices differently than the county's outer flanks, so we always check your specific section before quoting a number.

faqs.question: I have a small fractional interest split among several heirs. Is it still worth selling?
faqs.answer: Yes, we regularly buy small fractional interests. We confirm each heir's exact share through the county record and any applicable pooling order before making an offer.

faqs.question: How does SB 19-181 affect drilling in Weld County specifically?
faqs.answer: Weld County pursued Local Government Designee status to keep permitting review local and relatively efficient, which has helped it stay more predictable for operators than some neighboring counties that adopted stricter local setbacks.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Weld County sale close?
faqs.answer: Once we confirm your chain of title and current division order, most Weld County transactions close within two to four weeks.
